promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: The knee pain on Sunday is the one thing that matters this week, so get it looked at by a sports physio and we hold the hard work until it settles. Next week is deliberately light and flat so you can test the leg without digging a hole.

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
- I can't tell you what the knee is, and I won't guess. Lateral knee pain that is sharp on downhills, worsens as a run goes on, and still bothers you on stairs the next day is worth a visit to a sports physio or sports doc this week. Please book that in and let me know what they say.
- No tempo on Wednesday. We swap it for an easy run or a bike/pool session, keep everything flat, and only run if the knee is quiet. We can rebuild the quality next week once the leg is behaving.

new.analysis:
## How the week actually went
You followed the plan on Tue, Thu and Sat, and the easy runs looked steady at 9:49/mi around 138 bpm. The Wednesday session hit the right average pace but as seven short reps rather than one 4 mi block, so you got less continuous time at threshold than I was after. The long run is where the week turned: knee pain from mile 7, 9 mi instead of 13, and a walk home.

## Why I'm pulling back
A new, sharp, side-of-the-knee pain that gets worse on downhills and lingers on stairs is a signal, not noise. We are 10 weeks out, and one careful week now is a much better trade than pushing into something that gets worse. That means no tempo, flatter routes, a shorter long run, and a hard rule to stop if the knee gets sharp.

## What next week is doing
Volume drops to the mid 20s, every run is flat, and Wednesday becomes easy or cross-training so there is no load spike. The Sunday long run is 8 mi, flat, heart rate under 150, with permission to stop and walk if the knee flares. If the physio clears you and the leg stays quiet, we rebuild the long run and bring back a threshold session the following week.

## What to tell me on the next check-in
How the physio visit went and what they said about running. Whether the knee was quiet, grumbly or sharp on each run, and on stairs the next morning. That will decide how quickly we return to a 13 – 14 mi long run and a proper tempo.

safetyCallouts.title: See a sports physio about the right knee.
safetyCallouts.body: A new, sharp, side-of-the-knee pain that worsens through a run and still bothers you on stairs the next day is worth getting checked this week before loading it again. Please stop any run if the pain turns sharp, and do not run through it to finish a session.
